canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.name: Choy sum soup with minced pork
aliases: Choy sum and minced pork soup
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.serving_basis: About three bowls of clear soup for a family meal.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.description: Tender choy sum cooks briefly in a light broth with loose pieces of minced pork and scallion. This familiar soup is quick to prepare and pairs well with steamed rice.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.finished_dish: A clear, mild broth with tender pork and bright green choy sum that is cooked just until done.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.excerpt: A clear, mild broth with tender pork and bright green choy sum that is cooked just until done.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice; it pairs well with braised fish or another simple main dish.
tips: Stir gently when adding the pork to boiling water so it separates into small pieces.
Add the greens when the broth is boiling and cook for only 2–3 minutes to prevent them from becoming too soft.
Season with fish sauce a little at a time near the end.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.tip: Stir gently when adding the pork to boiling water so it separates into small pieces.
search_terms: Choy sum soup with minced pork
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.image_alt: Choy sum soup with minced pork in a white ceramic bowl; original Bếp Việt dish artwork.
preparation_steps: Trim any wilted leaves and wash the choy sum well. Cut into bite-sized lengths and drain.
Make sure the ground pork is ready and drain off excess moisture. Crush or mince the scallion roots.
Chop the scallion leaves and set aside to garnish the soup.
cooking_steps: Bring the water to a boil. Add the oil, crushed scallion root and minced pork, stirring gently to separate the meat.
When the broth returns to a boil, skim the surface and add the choy sum.
Season with fish sauce, salt, sugar and optional monosodium glutamate. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the greens are just tender, taste and turn off the heat.
Finish with ground pepper and scallion. Avoid overcooking to keep the greens bright and lightly crisp.
canh-cai-ngot-thit-bam.time_note: Estimated preparation and cooking time; cook the greens only until tender to retain their color and texture.

goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.name: Nam O Fish Salad, Da Nang
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.serving_basis: Four portions of dry-style herring salad wrapped with edible wild greens and rice paper, served with cooked Nam O dipping sauce.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.description: A specialty of the Nam O fishing village, made with thin herring fillets mixed with toasted rice powder, galangal, ginger and sesame. Wrap with edible wild greens and rice paper, then dip in a thick Nam O fish sauce.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.finished_dish: Chilled herring is nutty and fragrant with toasted rice powder, galangal, ginger and sesame. Edible wild greens balance the fish; cooked Nam O dipping sauce is savory, lightly sweet and spicy.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.serving: Serve the fish and dipping sauce separately with edible greens and rice paper. Wrap each bite as you eat and serve promptly while the fish is cold.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.image_alt: Dry-style Nam O fish salad with herring coated in toasted rice powder, edible wild greens, rice paper and Nam O dipping sauce.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.time_note: Editorial estimate; actual time depends on fish preparation and available greens.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.recipe_family: Nam O Fish Salad, Da Nang

dry herring salad with toasted rice powder
rice paper and edible wild greens
tips: This is a raw-fish dish. Use fish from a trusted supplier who confirms it is suitable for raw consumption; keep chilled, use separate utensils and serve promptly.
Lime or vinegar adds the traditional tart flavor; it is not a safety treatment for raw fish.
If the fish source and handling cannot be confirmed, do not serve this raw version; cooked fish would be a different variation.

ingredients.notes: Use positively identified edible leaves or common raw-eating herbs.

preparation_steps: Keep fish chilled until preparation. Use a clean knife, board and bowl reserved for raw fish; check for bones, slice thinly and refrigerate.
Rinse greens under clean running water and drain well. Chop galangal, ginger, garlic and chili; crush peanuts and prepare rice paper.
Mix fish sauce with water, galangal, ginger, garlic, chili and sugar. Bring to a full boil, reduce the heat and stir in toasted rice powder gradually until thick; season and cool.
cooking_steps: Place fish in a chilled bowl and add enough lime juice for the salad's tart flavor. Keep briefly refrigerated and drain. Lime does not replace the need to choose fish suitable for raw consumption.
Mix fish with galangal, ginger, toasted rice powder, sesame and some peanuts. Keep chilled until just before serving.
Arrange fish, greens, rice paper, rice crackers and sauce separately. Wrap each bite as eaten, dip and serve immediately; do not leave raw fish at room temperature.

ca-loc-kho-chuoi-xanh.name: Snakehead fish braised with green bananas
aliases: Snakehead fish braised with green plantain
ca-loc-kho-chuoi-xanh.serving_basis: One family pot of braised snakehead fish and green bananas for four people.
ca-loc-kho-chuoi-xanh.description: Snakehead fish is marinated with fish sauce, pepper and chili, then braised with green bananas until both absorb a light caramel glaze. Bếp Việt adapts the method for a home kitchen, keeping the bananas tender but intact and the sauce gently reduced.
ca-loc-kho-chuoi-xanh.finished_dish: Firm, tender fish pieces nestled among golden-brown green banana chunks in a glossy, savory-sweet braising sauce.
ca-loc-kho-chuoi-xanh.serving: Arrange the fish and bananas in a shallow dish, spoon over a little sauce and serve hot with steamed rice and boiled vegetables.
tips: Soak cut green bananas in salted lemon water to slow discoloration.
Marinate the fish for about 30 minutes and sear it briefly before adding liquid.
Braise over low heat, add hot water as needed and avoid vigorous stirring.

preparation_steps: Rinse and cut the fish into steaks. Rub lightly with salt and vinegar, rinse again and pat dry.
Lightly peel and cut the bananas; soak them in salted water with lime juice.
Mince garlic, slice shallots and chili. Marinate the fish with fish sauce, pepper, chili sauce, sugar, garlic and chili for 30 minutes.
cooking_steps: Caramelize part of the sugar with a little water until amber, then add oil and fry the shallots until fragrant.
Sear both sides of the fish until firm. Add the bananas and remaining marinade, turning gently to coat.
Pour in hot water to nearly cover the fish. Bring to a gentle boil, cover and braise on low heat for 25–30 minutes, until the bananas are tender and the sauce has reduced.

ca-tre-kho-gung.name: Vietnamese catfish braised with ginger
aliases: Catfish braised with ginger and coconut water
ca-tre-kho-gung.serving_basis: Four servings of catfish braised with young ginger and fresh coconut water.
ca-tre-kho-gung.description: Catfish is marinated with fish sauce, caramel and pepper, then braised with young ginger in fresh coconut water. Bep Viet adapts the documented method for a family meal, finishing the sauce with a little rice flour for a light gloss.
ca-tre-kho-gung.finished_dish: Tender, firm catfish pieces in a glossy amber coconut sauce with young ginger, shallots and chili.
ca-tre-kho-gung.serving: Serve from the clay pot or transfer to a shallow dish. Spoon the sauce over the fish and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Choose young ginger for a fragrant flavor without bitterness.
Marinate the fish for about 20 minutes before braising.
Mix rice flour with a little water and add it after the fish is cooked; stop when the sauce is lightly thickened.
search_terms: Braised fish dish served with rice

ca-tre-kho-gung.time_note: About 1 hour and 15 minutes, including 20 minutes of marinating.

ingredients.notes: Cut into pieces about 2 cm thick and drain.

ingredients.notes: Crush or leave whole according to heat preference.

preparation_steps: Clean the catfish, rub with salt to remove slime and odor, rinse and cut into thick pieces.
Rinse the young ginger and slice it. Mince the shallots and crush the chilies.
Marinate the fish with fish sauce, salt, sugar, pepper and caramel sauce for about 20 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat oil in a clay pot and fry the shallots until fragrant. Add the fish and turn gently until the surface firms; pour in the marinade.
Add coconut water, bring to a boil and skim. Lower the heat, add ginger and chili, then braise gently until the fish is cooked and the sauce has reduced. Turn the fish carefully.
Mix rice flour with water, pour it into the pot gradually and simmer until the sauce lightly thickens. Taste, finish with pepper and turn off the heat.

ca-nuong-rieng-me.name: Northern Vietnamese grilled fish with galangal and fermented rice
aliases: Grilled carp with galangal and fermented rice
ca-nuong-rieng-me.serving_basis: One fish around 900 g, divided among four and served with rice or vermicelli and fresh herbs.
ca-nuong-rieng-me.description: Carp is marinated with galangal, lemongrass, turmeric and fermented rice, then grilled until fragrant and golden while the flesh stays moist. This Northern Vietnamese home-style dish is served with herbs and a dipping sauce.
ca-nuong-rieng-me.finished_dish: Golden grilled carp with a fragrant galangal and lemongrass crust, tender flesh, gentle tang from fermented rice and optional chili heat.
ca-nuong-rieng-me.excerpt: Whole carp marinated with galangal, lemongrass and fermented rice, grilled until golden and served with herbs.
ca-nuong-rieng-me.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice or vermicelli, fresh herbs and a sweet-sour fish sauce dip with garlic and chili.
tips: Score the fish shallowly on both sides so the marinade reaches the flesh and it grills evenly.
Marinate in the refrigerator for at least one hour; do not leave raw fish at room temperature for an extended period.
Grilling time varies with fish size and equipment; check the thickest part is cooked before serving.
ca-nuong-rieng-me.tip: Grilling time varies with fish size and equipment; check the thickest part is cooked before serving.
ca-nuong-rieng-me.image_alt: Whole Vietnamese grilled carp marinated with galangal and fermented rice on a blue-and-white platter with herbs; original Bếp Việt artwork.
preparation_steps: Clean the fish, remove the gills and innards, rub lightly with salt and lime, rinse and pat dry. Score a few shallow diagonal cuts on both sides.
Pound or grind the galangal, lemongrass, turmeric, shallot and garlic. Strain the fermented rice starter.

Mix the aromatics with fermented rice, shrimp paste, fish sauce, sugar, seasoning powder, pepper and some of the oil. Rub over the fish and inside the cavity; cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Wash and drain the fresh herbs. Mix fish sauce for dipping with water, sugar, lime, minced garlic and chili.
cooking_steps: Heat the oven to about 200°C or prepare a charcoal grill. Lightly oil the rack and place the fish on it.
Grill, turning once and brushing with a little oil if needed. Adjust the time to the size of the fish and the equipment; check the thickest part and avoid scorching or drying the flesh.
Serve the fish hot with herbs, vermicelli or steamed rice and the dipping sauce.
ca-nuong-rieng-me.time_note: Marinate the fish under refrigeration. Grilling time is an estimate and varies with fish size, oven and charcoal heat.

ca-dieu-hong-hap-hanh-gung.name: Steamed red tilapia with ginger and scallions
aliases: Ginger and scallion steamed red tilapia
ca-dieu-hong-hap-hanh-gung.serving_basis: One 800–900 g red tilapia steamed with ginger and scallions for four people.
ca-dieu-hong-hap-hanh-gung.description: Red tilapia stays moist and tender, scented with ginger and scallions in a gently seasoned sauce. This Bếp Việt family version keeps the sauce measured and serves the steaming juices with rice or noodles.
ca-dieu-hong-hap-hanh-gung.finished_dish: The thickest flesh is opaque and flakes easily while remaining moist; ginger and scallions are aromatic, with a lightly glossy sauce.
ca-dieu-hong-hap-hanh-gung.serving: Set the fish on a deep platter, spoon over the sauce and juices, and finish with fried shallots and herbs. Serve with rice or rice vermicelli.
tips: Preheat the steamer and bring the water to a boil before adding the fish.
Check that the thickest section reaches 63°C or is opaque and flakes easily; avoid oversteaming.

ca-dieu-hong-hap-hanh-gung.time_note: About 75 minutes including a 10-minute marinade; steaming depends on size and thickness.

preparation_steps: Rinse and pat the fish dry; score both sides. Lightly season with soy sauce and pepper for about 10 minutes.
Slice ginger and shallots, cut chili, mince garlic, and prepare a heatproof platter and steamer.
cooking_steps: Fry garlic until fragrant; stir in soy sauces, oyster sauce, sugar, sesame oil and water. Add ginger and shallots, simmer briefly, then turn off the heat.
Line the platter with ginger and scallion whites, add the fish and sauce, and steam covered for about 35–40 minutes, depending on size.
Check the thickest section; add scallions, cilantro and chili, steam 1–2 minutes more, and finish with fried shallots.

bi-do-xao-toi.name: Vietnamese garlic stir-fried pumpkin
bi-do-xao-toi.serving_basis: One family-style plate of stir-fried pumpkin with garlic for four people.
bi-do-xao-toi.description: Pumpkin is quickly stir-fried with garlic, then covered briefly with a little water until just tender. The pieces stay intact and retain their naturally sweet, nutty flavor, making a simple weeknight vegetable side.
bi-do-xao-toi.finished_dish: Tender but intact pumpkin, lightly coated with fragrant garlic and finished with cilantro.
bi-do-xao-toi.serving: Transfer to a plate, scatter with cilantro and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Cut pumpkin evenly and add water a little at a time.
Cover briefly over low heat and stop cooking once tender.
bi-do-xao-toi.image_alt: Vietnamese stir-fried pumpkin with minced garlic and cilantro on a ceramic plate.
bi-do-xao-toi.time_note: About 15 minutes from preparation to serving.

preparation_steps: Peel pumpkin, remove seeds and fibers, cut into even pieces, rinse and drain.
Crush and mince garlic; rinse and drain cilantro.
cooking_steps: Heat oil over medium heat and sauté garlic until fragrant. Add pumpkin and toss to coat.
Season with seasoning powder, a little sugar and salt; toss for about 2 minutes.
Add water, cover and cook over low heat for 2–4 minutes until just tender. Finish with cilantro and serve.

mien-luon-nghe-an.name: Nghe An eel glass-noodle soup
mien-luon-nghe-an.serving_basis: Four bowls of eel glass noodles with bone broth, crispy eel and sautéed eel.
mien-luon-nghe-an.description: Nghệ An eel glass-noodle soup combines glass noodles and freshwater eel with a turmeric-scented pork-bone broth and local shallots. Bếp Việt serves the eel in two textures: a lightly coated crisp portion and a soft sautéed portion.
mien-luon-nghe-an.finished_dish: A bowl of translucent glass noodles in golden broth, topped with golden eel, scallions and Vietnamese coriander.
mien-luon-nghe-an.serving: Soften the glass noodles, divide them among bowls and arrange the crispy and sautéed eel on top. Pour over hot broth and finish with scallions, Vietnamese coriander and pepper.
tips: Clean the eel thoroughly and remove any bones before serving.
Use only a thin flour coating so the fried eel stays crisp without becoming heavy.
Soak glass noodles according to the package and blanch separately to keep the broth clear.
mien-luon-nghe-an.image_alt: Nghệ An eel glass-noodle soup with golden eel, glass noodles, herbs and turmeric broth.
mien-luon-nghe-an.time_note: About 1 hour and 45 minutes, including broth simmering and noodle soaking.

ingredients.name: Cleaned freshwater eel
ingredients.notes: Fillet the meat; reserve bones if using them for broth.

ingredients.name: Glass noodles
ingredients.notes: Soak until pliable according to the package.

ingredients.name: Crispy-frying flour
ingredients.notes: Use a thin coating for part of the eel.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Bruise and add to the broth.

ingredients.name: Fresh turmeric
ingredients.notes: Crush for its juice or mince finely.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil

preparation_steps: Blanch the pork bones and rinse. Clean and fillet the eel, keeping bones separate if using them for broth; check carefully for small bones.
Soak the glass noodles until pliable and drain. Crush turmeric for its juice; mince the Vietnamese shallots and shallots, and bruise the ginger.
Divide the eel into two portions. Season both with turmeric, fish sauce, salt and pepper; lightly coat one portion with frying flour.
cooking_steps: Simmer the pork bones with ginger and turmeric for about 45 minutes, skimming regularly. Season the broth with fish sauce, salt and pepper.
Fry the coated eel until golden and drain. Fry the Vietnamese shallots and shallots until fragrant, then quickly sauté the remaining eel until just cooked.
Blanch the glass noodles until just tender and divide among bowls. Add both styles of eel and pour over the hot broth.
Finish with scallions, Vietnamese coriander and pepper; serve immediately.
